text:
Carla Mendez: Hey team — customer AcmeHealth is ready to wrap the POC. We need a clear handback plan: VPC handoff, invalidate hosted API keys, and teardown the dedicated pool. Any objections to a phased handback tomorrow 09:00 UTC?

Benji Liu: I can own the dedicated pool teardown. Which pool ID are we targeting?

Carla Mendez: Pool ID: dp-77b1. They asked for 30-day logs retention in the initial request but Legal flagged 90 days for some telemetry. @Anika any guidance?

Anika Rao: Legal confirmed 30 days is fine for the POC artifacts; 90 days is only for production engagements.

Legal Bot: policy: POC_DATA_RETENTION=30d (automated note)

infra-bot: Heads up — teardown requires no active routes. Suggested commands: `rwctl routes list --pool dp-77b1` then `rwctl pool drain --id dp-77b1` and `rwctl pool destroy --id dp-77b1` once drained.

Benji Liu: I'll start the drain at 08:30 UTC and plan teardown at 09:00 if there are no active connections or errors.

Carla Mendez: Hosted API keys: we issued keys for acme-poc-user: `sk_live_acme1234` and `sk_live_acme-old`. Do we rotate or fully revoke? What's the impact on their logs / replayability?

SRE Oncall: Revoke both keys. If they request further access later, issue ephemeral keys with short TTL. Revoke via API: `POST /v1/keys/revoke { \"key_id\": \"<key>\" }` or use Console -> Security -> API Keys.

Anika Rao: Also make sure to snapshot embeddings + KV cache used for the POC (customer asked for a copy). Store in secure S3 with lifecycle policy to auto-delete after 30 days. Carla — which bucket prefix?

Carla Mendez: Use `s3://redwood-poc-handbacks/acmehealth-17999`. Set metadata `legal_hold=false` and ACL to restrict to redwood-poc-handbacks-admins.

Benji Liu: After key revocation I'll verify there are no active connections to the pool and post the drain logs. I'll also confirm the snapshot completed before destroy.

Carla Mendez: VPC handoff checklist we need to run: remove VPC peering, revoke service principals, return route tables, ensure SGs narrow to no ingress from customer IPs. Who will do the VPC steps?

Benji Liu: I'll coordinate with the customer's network lead. I need their ASN and peering id to schedule the peering deletion.

Carla Mendez: ASN=65012, peering-id=peer-0a1b2c (from their network team).

infra-bot: Action created: `#teardown-acmehealth-1799960010` assigned to Benji Liu. ETA: 2026-03-22 09:00 UTC.

Benji Liu: Noted. A couple of operational notes: preserve prompt sets and eval artifacts for 30 days in the bucket, then auto-delete. Also ensure Dedicated billing stops as of teardown time — I'll ask Finance for stop date.

Carla Mendez: FYI on pricing: POC committed credits unused = $2,400. Finance confirmed they can credit back after teardown; they'll need the invoice id and teardown confirmation.

Carla Mendez: Quick checklist for tomorrow: 
- [ ] Drain dp-77b1
- [ ] Revoke API keys for acme-poc-user
- [ ] Snapshot KV + embeddings -> s3://redwood-poc-handbacks/acmehealth-17999
- [ ] Remove VPC peering (peer-0a1b2c) and close SGs
- [ ] Destroy dedicated pool dp-77b1
- [ ] Confirm billing stop and issue credit
- [ ] Send final handback email to customer with artifact links and retention policy

Benji Liu: I'll tick items as I do them and post logs. :thumbsup:

Carla Mendez: Thanks — @SRE Oncall please monitor the platform for 2 hours post-teardown for any anomaly alerts and escalate if anything pops up.

SRE Oncall: Will monitor. I’ll keep the incident channel open for 2 hours post-ETA and notify if any token handoff/queue backlog occurs.

Benji Liu: Update 08:45 UTC — started drain, one long-lived connection from customer agent-23. Reached out to their contact to close.

Carla Mendez: Great. Keep us posted. Once all done I'll send the formal handback note and attach the S3 links + retention policy.
